title: FUSIS: Fusing Surrogate Models and Importance Sampling for Efficient Yield Estimation
problem: Yield estimation faces a fundamental tradeoff: surrogate models are fast but often inaccurate and not robust; importance sampling is accurate but computationally expensive. Both methods suffer individually at advanced process nodes.
motivation: Yield estimation is increasingly critical as process nodes shrink; existing approaches cannot achieve both speed and accuracy simultaneously.
method: Unified FUSIS framework combines surrogate and importance sampling strengths: (1) Deep Kernel SVM approximates the indicator function (determines yield/fail); (2) Uses SVM as proposal distribution for importance sampling to accelerate convergence; (3) Correction factor adjusts yield estimate to mitigate surrogate inaccuracies. Evaluated on SRAM and analog circuits.
key_novelty: Fusion of surrogate-based and IS-based approaches where surrogates guide optimal IS proposal distribution, achieving both robustness and efficiency.
contributions: Up to 24.84% accuracy improvement (8.67% average) vs state-of-the-art
Up to 29.54x speedup (10.30x average) in efficiency
Mitigates both surrogate inaccuracy and IS sampling overhead
Applicable to SRAM and analog circuits
limitations: Evaluation limited to SRAM and analog circuits; applicability to digital logic and mixed-signal designs not demonstrated.
primary_theme: surrogate-IS fusion for robust efficient yield estimation
